name: blemished king

attributes.attribute: a mythic theme among the Celts
a king must be whole to wed the land goddess
lost his arm at the first Battle of Mag Tuired
gave up leadership of the Tuatha De Danann until given a prosthesis
legend based on the blemished king motif

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The blemished king is a mythic theme. A king could wed the land goddess only if whole. Through her he claimed the sovereignty of the country. Injury forced him to give up the throne. Nuada lost an arm in the first conflict at Mag Tuired. He then yielded leadership of the Tuatha De Danann. A magical prosthesis let him return. The motif underlies the Fisher King legends in the Arthurian cycle.

okr.objective: Describe the blemished king theme and how injury forced a king from the throne.
key_results: A king could claim the land goddess only if unblemished.
Injury forced the king to abdicate.
Nuada lost his arm at the first Battle of Mag Tuired.
The motif grounds the Fisher King legends.
